title: 7.4 A 112Gb/s DSP-Based PAM-4 Receiver with an LC-Resonator-Based CTLE for >52dB Loss Compensation in 4nm FinFET
problem: High-speed wireline transceivers (100Gb/s+) for AI/GPU interconnects and PCIe 7.0 require signal recovery over long channels with severe channel loss (>52dB). Traditional Continuous-Time Linear Equalization (CTLE) struggles with high-loss channels; existing DSP-based receivers lack energy-efficient, broadband equalization architectures.
method: DSP-based 112Gb/s PAM-4 receiver with novel LC-resonator-based CTLE providing >52dB loss compensation. Architecture combines: (1) LC-resonator front-end achieving broadband peaking/gain without power-hungry analog inductors; (2) DSP backend for adaptive equalization and PAM-4 symbol detection; (3) latency reduction techniques (analog data path optimization) minimizing overall receive latency. 4nm FinFET implementation achieves energy efficiency suitable for data-center deployment.

title: QPRAC: Towards Secure and Practical PRAC-based Rowhammer Mitigation using Priority Queues
problem: The JEDEC PRAC (Per Row Activation Counting) framework for DDR5 enables RowHammer mitigation via Alert Back-Off (ABO) signaling, but existing PRAC implementations (e.g., Panopticon) are either insecure when instantiated per JEDEC specification, or impractical (e.g., UPRAC) due to requiring oracle knowledge of the top-N most-activated rows.
method: QPRAC designs a Priority-based Service Queue (PSQ) in the memory controller that maintains pending mitigation requests sorted by row activation count, using PRAC's per-row counters to prioritize mitigations. High activation-count rows are served first, preventing adversarial bypass. The PSQ is co-designed with two complementary mechanisms: opportunistic mitigation during Refresh Management (RFM) operations (piggybacking extra mitigations at low cost), and proactive mitigation during standard DRAM refresh (REF) operations to drain the queue before ABO events fire, minimizing performance impact.

title: FRED: A Wafer-scale Fabric for 3D Parallel DNN Training
problem: Current wafer-scale interconnect topologies (e.g., 2D mesh) lack the flexibility to simultaneously support tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism in DNN training, causing collective communications to contend for shared links and inflating training time.
method: FRED introduces a distributed on-wafer topology built from tiny microswitches interconnecting accelerator chiplets on the wafer. The microswitches form a reconfigurable, nonblocking network that can route collective communications (all-reduce, all-to-all) between arbitrary subsets of chiplets without interference. In-switch collective support allows reduction operations to be partially executed at intermediate network nodes, reducing traffic volume. This topology is tailored so that different parallelism dimensions (data, tensor, pipeline) map to non-overlapping logical groups with dedicated bandwidth.

title: A 1.11pJ/b 224Gb/s XSR Receiver with Slice-Based CTLE and PI-Based Clock Generator in 12nm CMOS
problem: Extra-short reach (XSR) 224Gb/s receivers at 112Gb/s-equivalent require both CTLE bandwidth doubling and 8x sampling frequency increase while maintaining strict power and area constraints.
method: Extra-short reach receiver using slice-based continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) and phase-interpolator (PI)-based eight-phase clock generator, enabling efficient bandwidth scaling in 12nm CMOS. Slicing CTLE distributes filtering across multiple stages.

title: ZK-Hammer: Leaking Secrets from Zero-Knowledge Proofs via Rowhammer
problem: Zero-knowledge SNARK schemes are assumed cryptographically secure but their vulnerability to fault injection attacks via Rowhammer is unexplored, potentially compromising secret exponents.
method: ZK-Hammer induces Rowhammer faults into exponentiate variables in the Quadratic Arithmetic Program (QAP) representation of zk-SNARK proofs, then analyzes faulty proofs using bilinear pairing techniques to recover secret parameters.

title: STREAM: Spatiotemporal Similarity-based Efficient Approximate Median with Tunable Granularity
problem: Exact median computation is expensive and fails to meet near real-time requirements; existing approximate methods ignore spatiotemporal data characteristics and lack application-specific accuracy-speed trade-offs.
method: STREAM exploits spatiotemporal similarity in data streams to achieve bucket reuse via streaming K-means-like clustering. Introduces tunable-grained bucket mechanism allowing application-specific trade-offs between execution time and accuracy. Uses prior bucket state to accelerate median estimation.

title: Towards Secure Data Management using Multi-Cryptographic Solutions (Invited)
problem: Secure data outsourcing systems incorporate various cryptographic techniques, but their security properties are often ad hoc and obscure, making it difficult to reason about unintended information leakage.
method: Secure Normal Form (SNF) framework enabling data owners to define acceptable leakages for non-sensitive data aspects, allowing efficient query processing while guaranteeing no unintended sensitive information leakage. The paper discusses SNF application to advanced computational environments and modern data management architectures.

title: Construction of DAG Models for Autonomous Systems
problem: Constructing optimal directed acyclic graph (DAG) task models for autonomous systems (vehicles, drones) to minimize end-to-end response time, particularly for time-triggered blended task chains.
method: Proposes representation semantics for time-triggered task chains in autonomous systems and introduces a topology optimization method that improves average end-to-end response time by 4.8x compared to Floyd algorithm with O(n²) complexity suitable for dynamic task handling.

title: 26.2 A Wideband Replicas-Rejection Digital Transmitter Using Joint-Digital-Analog Interpolation and Filtering in 28nm CMOS
problem: Wideband digital transmitters (DTXs) struggle with sampling replicas at f_LO + n×f_s that fall close to signal band, violating emission masks and requiring high sampling rates + expensive off-chip RF filters. Supporting multiple sub-6 GHz standards (LB/HB) forces separate RF chains, increasing area and complexity.
method: Joint digital-analog interpolation and filtering strategy: optimized digital polyphase filter reduces per-channel sampling rate while maintaining high output rate; wideband quadrature DPA with IQ-cell-sharing and transformer-based load modulation; analog interpolation integrated into DPA circuit to suppress replicas. Unified architecture eliminates need for separate LB/HB chains.

title: BLOOM: Bit-Slice Framework for DNN Acceleration with Mixed-Precision
problem: INT4 quantization limited by outliers (high-magnitude values); existing outlier-aware compression adds complex serialization/deserialization logic that dominates execution time, reducing speedup.
method: Bit-slicing framework exploiting outlier-precision separation: outliers retain higher precision (INT8), normal values use INT4; interleaved bit-level storage exposes sparsity in high-precision components, enabling adaptive dataflow with minimal serialization overhead.

title: Efficient Lossless Compression of Scientific Floating-Point Data on CPUs and GPUs
problem: Scientific datasets are growing faster than storage and interconnect bandwidth, making data compression essential, but existing lossless compressors for floating-point data are either fast or achieve good compression ratios—rarely both simultaneously on both CPUs and GPUs.
method: The paper presents four new lossless compression algorithms specifically designed for single- and double-precision IEEE 754 floating-point data. The algorithms are fully compatible between CPUs and GPUs, enabling the same bitstream to be produced/consumed on either platform. Implementations exploit bit-level patterns in floating-point exponent and mantissa fields to achieve high compression ratios, and are tuned for SIMD/SIMT parallelism to maximize throughput on both CPU vector units and GPU streaming multiprocessors. Evaluated against 18 compressors from the literature on SDRBench scientific datasets.

title: 33.2 A 216-to-226GHz Watt-Level GaN Solid-State Power Amplifier with Multiband Large-Signal Impedance Correction and Circuit-Package Co-Design Technique
problem: 220GHz solid-state power amplifiers (SSPAs) are critical for future high-data-rate wireless, imaging, and radar; Si (CMOS/SiGe) and III-V (GaAs/InP) PAs suffer from low operating voltage (<2V single device), requiring low impedance at output (high current), limiting bandwidth and power density. GaN HEMTs offer higher voltage/current ratings but design is challenging at G-band.
method: GaN HEMT-based 216–226GHz SSPA using: (1) multiband large-signal impedance correction to optimize output impedance across the G-band range despite device parasitics, (2) circuit-package co-design enabling efficient coupling from PA to antenna/load while managing thermal and parasitic effects.

title: A 184.8dB-FoMs 1.6MS/s Incremental Noise-Shaping Pipeline ADC with Single-Amplification-Based kT/C Noise Cancellation Technique
problem: Incremental ADCs combining low-power SAR with high-resolution ΔΣ modulator suffer from slow conversion at high precision (kHz range); recent NS-SAR improves speed (300kS/s) but reduced oversampling ratio (OSR) causes sampling noise; kT/C noise cancellation requires static or repeatedly-triggered amplifiers, consuming power throughout entire conversion cycle.
method: Incremental noise-shaping pipeline ADC with single-amplification-based kT/C noise cancellation. Key innovation: amplifier remains active only during kT/C cancellation phase (not throughout conversion), drastically reducing power vs. prior approaches. Concurrent coarse and fine quantization stages without repeated sampling overhead.

title: DARIS: An Oversubscribed Spatio-Temporal Scheduler for Real-Time DNN Inference on GPUs
problem: GPUs face underutilization in DNN inference workloads due to coarse-grained scheduling that cannot exploit fine-grained spatial and temporal concurrency.
method: DARIS uses priority-based real-time scheduling combining NVIDIA MPS (Multi-Process Service) for spatial sharing and CUDA streaming for temporal partitioning. Synchronization-based staging enables zero-delay DNN migration between GPU partitions. Oversubscription mechanism analyzes GPU concurrency.

title: Robustness Verification for Checking Crash Consistency of Non-volatile Memory
problem: Programs using non-volatile memory (NVM) must explicitly flush pending stores to guarantee persistence; developers routinely miss or mis-order these flushes. Existing crash-consistency checkers are testing-based and require user guidance, leaving the correctness of NVM programs unverified in the general case.
method: The paper introduces a robustness property for NVM crash consistency and proves that checking whether a post-crash NVM state is reachable from a given pre-crash execution reduces to validity of that execution under additional ordering constraints. A search-based algorithm enumerates all partial pre-crash executions and candidate NVM states, then dispatches each reachability query to an SMT solver via symbolic encoding of the program. The approach is integrated into the DPLL(T) framework to prune the search space, and is implemented in the prototype tool PMVerify.

title: 19.3 A Fractional-N PLL with 34fsrms Jitter and -255.5dB FoM Based on a Multipath Feedback Technique
problem: Advanced wireless communication (4K-QAM and beyond) requires frequency synthesizers with sub-100 fs RMS jitter to meet stringent phase-noise requirements. Prior fractional-N PLLs achieve excellent jitter but rely on impractically high reference frequencies (150–500 MHz), unsuitable for cost-effective deployment.
method: Multipath feedback technique in an analog PLL architecture enables competitive jitter performance despite low 80 MHz reference frequency (7.5x lower than prior sub-100 fs designs). The technique exploits parallel feedback paths to reduce charge-pump dead-zone and reference spur injection, improving phase margin and jitter. PLL operates 7.3–9.5 GHz output range.
